doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: High school performing: Fats Waller, trumpet in the band, Victrola records
summary: He played Fats Waller's Hold Tight at assembly, played trumpet in the school band and heard Earl Hines records at a cousin's.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: In high school, were you performing at all?
No.
I gather you did do...
Well, I did a couple of tunes at... I played a Fats Waller tune at the assembly, where everybody got together... Jimmy Brazier won the thing, the “Washington and Lee Swing.”
I believe the Fats Waller tune you played was “Hold Tight.”
Yes.
At the time, when you were in high school, did you know a lot of repertoire?
I don’t know. I don’t know where...
You said that you played trumpet also in high school. That’s when you started playing trumpet.
Yes. I played trumpet in the band, in the high school band.
What sorts of things did the high school band played?
I don’t know. Souza.
Marches and so on.
Yes.
So it wasn’t “hot music,” as it was called then.
No. I used to play licks, you know, from the other stuff, in the band...in... I don’t know.
Was it in high school that Mariana introduced you to jazz?
No. Introduced...
To records. That she had records, your cousin...
Elizabeth Staton.
Elizabeth Staton, it was. Not Mariana Staton. Elizabeth.
Well, Elizabeth Staton had a wind-up Victrola with Earl Hines and...oh, a lot of other people. I listened to that for a while.
And obviously listened closely.

I just remember Fats Waller from that area. I did a tune by him, “Hold Tight,” and “Foo-ra-de-ack-a-sa-ki. Want some seafood, Mama.” I played it at the high school auditorium, and I lost the contest...
